name: sicilian pesto rosso
instructions:
Pesto rosso alla trapanese — the traditional sicilian red pesto. Raw blended sun-dried-tomato + almond + basil paste. No cook.

See sibling recipes in the italian-tomato-sauces folder ([[marcella-tomato-sauce]], [[vodka-sauce]], [[pasta-piperade]], [[marcella-eggplant-sauce]]) for other italian tomato-sauce shapes.

=== INGREDIENTS ===

- sun-dried tomatoes (rehydrated in warm water if dry-packed; drain and pat dry)
- almonds (blanched, unsalted)
- fresh basil leaves
- garlic (raw, 1-2 cloves)
- olive oil (good quality)
- pecorino cheese (traditional) or parmesan cheese
- salt
- red chili flakes (optional, traditional in some sicilian versions)
- pasta (short shapes like busiate traditionally; penne, fusilli, or trofie all work)

=== PROCEDURE ===

1. Rehydrate the sun-dried tomatoes if dry-packed. Skip if oil-packed.
2. In a food processor or blender, combine sun-dried tomatoes, almonds, basil, garlic, and a pinch of red chili flakes. Pulse to a rough paste.
3. With the motor running, drizzle in olive oil until the sauce reaches a thick, spreadable consistency — a loose paste, not a smooth sauce.
4. Fold in grated pecorino (or parmesan) and salt to taste. Fold in by hand off the blades — don't blend the cheese.
5. Toss with hot cooked pasta. Loosen with a splash of pasta water if too thick.
notes:
Traditional sicilian red pesto (pesto rosso alla trapanese). Split out from the former italian-tomato-sauces.json (Variant B) into its own file. Classical / traditional recipe — not one specific author.

=== SUN-DRIED TOMATOES ARE THE STRUCTURAL INGREDIENT — NOT TOMATO PASTE, NOT CANNED ===

The tomato base is specifically SUN-DRIED tomatoes. Their chewy, umami-forward, slightly sweet dried-fruit register is what makes this read as pesto rather than sauce. Tomato paste is too cooked/concentrated; canned tomatoes carry too much water for a raw blended paste.

=== ALMONDS ARE THE NUT — BLANCHED, UNSALTED ===

Pine nuts are for green pesto; almonds anchor red. Blanched (skins off) gives the cleanest color. Unsalted so you control the seasoning.

=== PINE NUTS ARE CLASHING — DIFFERENT PESTO ENTIRELY ===

Pine nuts belong in green pesto (see [[italian-green-sauce-and-pesto]]) where their delicate resiny sweetness bridges basil and parmesan. In a tomato base they get lost.

=== SUNFLOWER SEEDS ARE CLASHING — CHALKY IN RED SAUCES ===

Sunflower seeds work in green pesto but read CHALKY in red / tomato sauces. Tested and confirmed. Stick with almonds; skip sunflower seeds entirely. Same principle applies across all the italian-tomato-sauces siblings.

=== BASIL IS NON-OPTIONAL ===

Without fresh basil the dish reads underwhelming — just ground sun-dried tomatoes and almonds with cheese. Basil is what makes it a pesto rather than an italian-tomato-and-almond spread.

=== PECORINO IS TRADITIONAL; PARMESAN IS FINE ===

The classic sicilian version uses pecorino — sharper, saltier, sheep's-milk depth against the sweet sun-dried tomatoes. Parmesan works too and is more likely to be on hand; pecorino is the upgrade when you have it.

=== FOOD PROCESSOR OR BLENDER, NOT MORTAR ===

Red pesto wants a blender or food processor. Almonds are too hard to break down by hand with a pestle in reasonable time. Green pesto is a mortar dish; red pesto is a blender dish.

=== SHORT PASTA SHAPES ===

Sicilian tradition pairs pesto trapanese with busiate (a twisted pasta). Penne, fusilli, trofie, cavatelli, or orecchiette all work. Long strands (spaghetti, linguine) don't grip red pesto well.

=== IF YOU IMPROVISE WITH NUTS — TOASTED WALNUTS OR PEELED ALMONDS ===

Across all italian tomato sauces (siblings in this folder), toasted walnuts or peeled almonds are best if you're substituting nuts. Pine nuts + sunflower seeds stay clashing across this family.

=== SIBLING RECIPES (TOMATO PASTA SAUCE TAG) ===

- [[marcella-tomato-sauce]]: Marcella Hazan's 3-ingredient simmered tomato sauce.
- [[vodka-sauce]]: tomato paste + cream outlier.
- [[pasta-piperade]]: blended vegetable-tomato base.
- [[marcella-eggplant-sauce]]: fried eggplant + garlic-tomato.
